cevap: Netflix's global average monthly revenue per paying membership (ARM, its ARPU measure) was essentially flat over the six years: $10.82 in 2019, $10.91 in 2020, $11.67 in 2021, $11.76 in 2022, $11.64 in 2023 and $11.70 in 2024 - a cumulative rise of only about 8% (roughly 1.4% a year), with all of the gain coming in 2021. The 2019-2021 figures come from the FY2021 10-K (accession 0001065280-22-000036) and the 2022-2024 figures from the FY2024 10-K (accession 0001065280-25-000044). The flat consolidated line hides diverging regional trends: in the FY2024 10-K, UCAN ARM rose from $15.86 (2022) to $16.28 (2023) to $17.20 (2024), EMEA was $10.99 / $10.87 / $10.96, while LATAM fell from $8.48 to $8.66 to $8.24 and APAC fell from $8.50 to $7.64 to $7.29. So consolidated ARM was held down by geographic mix shift toward lower-priced regions and by FX (Netflix reports 2024 constant-currency ARM growth of 4% versus the 1% reported figure), while paid memberships grew from 167.1 million at end-2019 to 301.6 million at end-2024.

Elinor Mertz is Airbnb's Chief Financial Officer. She signed Airbnb's FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001559720-25-000010, filed 13 February 2025) as Chief Financial Officer and Principal Financial Officer. The same signature page shows Brian Chesky as CEO and David Bernstein as Chief Accounting Officer. This is the most recent annual report on file as of the 16 May 2025 cutoff.

Work, using only what was on file by 16 May 2025. Guidance: in the 17 April 2025 6-K (accession 0001046179-25-000035) TSMC guided Q2 2025 revenue to US$28.4-29.2 billion, i.e. a US$28.8 billion midpoint (FX assumption NT$32.5/US$). Base: the same release reports Q1 2025 (the March quarter) revenue of NT$839.25 billion / US$25.53 billion. Normal March-quarter-to-June-quarter seasonality over the last three years, taken from the Q2 press releases: Q2 2022 NT$534.14bn, +8.8% QoQ (USD +3.4%) - accession 0001564590-22-025726; Q2 2023 NT$480.84bn, -5.5% QoQ (USD -6.2%) - accession 0001628280-23-025146; Q2 2024 NT$673.51bn, +13.6% QoQ (USD +10.3%) - accession 0001046179-24-000083. Three-year average sequential growth is +5.6% in NT$ and +2.5% in USD. Applying that to Q1 2025 gives NT$839.25bn x 1.056 = about NT$886bn, or US$27.3bn at the guided NT$32.5 rate; on the USD series, US$25.53bn x 1.025 = about US$26.2bn. Versus the US$28.8bn midpoint that is a MISS of roughly 5% (NT$-based) to 9% (USD-based). Caveat that cuts the other way: the 9 May 2025 monthly revenue 6-K (accession 0001046179-25-000052) shows April 2025 revenue of NT$349.57 billion, +48.1% YoY, which implies April 2024 was about NT$236bn, i.e. 35% of Q2 2024's NT$673.51bn. If April holds that same 35% share of the quarter, Q2 2025 would be about NT$999bn, or US$30.7bn - a BEAT of about 7%. So plain March-quarter seasonality points to a mid-single-digit to high-single-digit percentage miss, but the one month of actual Q2 data already on file points to a beat; the honest conclusion is that the seasonality-only model is not reliable here because AI-driven demand is breaking the historical sequential pattern.

Airbnb's take rate (revenue divided by Gross Booking Value) has been essentially flat with a small upward drift: FY2022 revenue $8,399 million on GBV of $63,212 million = 13.29%; FY2023 revenue $9,917 million on GBV of $73,252 million = 13.54%; FY2024 revenue $11,102 million on GBV of $81,784 million = 13.57%. That is roughly +25 basis points from 2022 to 2023 and only +3 basis points from 2023 to 2024, so the platform is monetising bookings at a stable rate and revenue growth is being driven by volume and price rather than by higher fees. GBV figures are from the key business metrics tables in the FY2023 10-K (accession 0001559720-24-000006) and the FY2024 10-K (accession 0001559720-25-000010); revenue is the XBRL reported figure from the same annual reports.

Dividing Gross Booking Value by Nights and Experiences Booked gives an implied value per night/experience of about $160.6 in FY2022 ($63,212 million / 393.7 million), $163.4 in FY2023 ($73,252 million / 448.2 million) and about $166.4 in FY2024 ($81,784 million / 491.5 million; the 10-K table rounds nights to 492 million, which gives $166.2). That is roughly +1.8% in 2023 and +1.8% in 2024, a cumulative rise of about 3.6% over the two years, consistent with Airbnb's commentary that higher Average Daily Rate contributed to GBV growth alongside volume. Note this is GBV per night, which is inclusive of host earnings, service fees, cleaning fees and taxes, and it is diluted slightly by experiences being counted in the denominator. Source: key business metrics tables in the FY2023 10-K (accession 0001559720-24-000006) and FY2024 10-K (accession 0001559720-25-000010).

Per Note 14 (Capital Structure) of Allstate's FY2024 10-K (accession 0000899051-25-000015), as of 31 December 2024 Allstate had $500 million outstanding of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures. Terms: scheduled maturity date 15 May 2057 with a final maturity date of 15 May 2067; redeemable in whole or in part at any time on or after 15 May 2037 at principal plus accrued and unpaid interest, and in certain circumstances before 15 May 2037 at principal plus accrued interest or, if greater, a make-whole price. Interest is payable semi-annually at the fixed 6.500% rate to 15 May 2037, and thereafter quarterly at three-month LIBOR plus 2.120%, with LIBOR replaced by the CME Term SOFR reference rate for a three-month tenor plus a 0.26161% spread adjustment. Allstate may defer interest for one or more consecutive periods not exceeding 10 years, with interest compounding during deferral; the deferral feature obliges Allstate in certain circumstances to issue common stock or other qualifying securities to fund the deferred interest, and 75 million authorised and unissued shares are reserved for that purpose. While interest is deferred, Allstate is prohibited from declaring or paying dividends or distributions on common or preferred stock or from redeeming or repurchasing such stock, subject to limited exceptions (Allstate did not defer interest in 2024). The debentures are also covered by a replacement capital covenant running to 2067 for the benefit of holders of the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053, under which Allstate will not repay, redeem or purchase the Junior Subordinated Debentures unless it has received specified net cash proceeds from sales of common stock or other qualifying securities, with carve-outs including an S&P upgrade to A or above, a tax-event redemption, and repurchases of up to 10% of principal in any one year (25% in any ten years). Rating agencies give the instrument partial equity credit in Allstate's capital structure. The $500 million balance was unchanged from 31 December 2023.

From loanDepot's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2024, filed 12 November 2024 (accession 0001831631-24-000285), loan originations by purpose for the nine months ended 30 September 2024 were: purchase $12,057,993 thousand (about $12.06 billion) and refinance $5,250,321 thousand (about $5.25 billion), for total originations of $17,308,314 thousand (about $17.31 billion). That is a mix of roughly 69.7% purchase and 30.3% refinance. For comparison, the same nine-month period in 2023 was purchase $12,403,166 thousand and refinance $4,897,857 thousand on total originations of $17,301,023 thousand (71.7% purchase / 28.3% refinance), so total volume was essentially flat year over year while the mix shifted modestly toward refinance. For the third quarter alone, purchase was $4,378,575 thousand and refinance $2,280,754 thousand on $6,659,329 thousand of total originations.

Warner Bros. Discovery does not disclose a single cumulative merger-restructuring total, but Note 6 of its FY2024 10-K (accession 0001437107-25-000031) states that the restructuring programme was launched in connection with the completion of the 8 April 2022 Merger with AT&T's WarnerMedia business and that the merger-related restructuring programme was considered substantially completed as of 31 December 2024. Summing the restructuring and other charges reported for the programme period gives $3,757 million in 2022 plus $585 million in 2023 plus $447 million in 2024, i.e. approximately $4,789 million (about $4.8 billion) of restructuring and other charges from the merger through 31 December 2024. By segment the 2022/2023/2024 charges were Studios $1,050m/$225m/$263m, Networks $1,003m/$201m/$85m, DTC $1,551m/$66m/$3m and Corporate and inter-segment eliminations $153m/$93m/$96m. Two caveats: the 2023 and 2024 amounts also include some non-merger initiatives (the 2023 Warner Bros. Pictures Animation realignment and, in 2024, an organisational and personnel restructuring plan and a Warner Bros. Games restructuring), and a further $411 million of facility consolidation impairment charges in 2024 was recorded in impairment and loss on dispositions rather than in restructuring and other charges. The restructuring liability balance fell from $864 million at end-2022 to $460 million at end-2023 and $289 million at end-2024, with cash paid of $853 million in 2023 and $423 million in 2024.

Using FY2024 cash dividends paid divided by net income attributable to the parent (both from the companies' FY2024 XBRL data as reported in their FY2024 10-Ks), the ranking from highest to lowest payout ratio is: 1) Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) 82.9% ($1,194 million of dividends on $1,441 million of net income); 2) Coca-Cola (KO) 78.6% ($8,359 million on $10,631 million); 3) PepsiCo (PEP) 75.5% ($7,229 million on $9,578 million); 4) Monster Beverage (MNST) 0%, as Monster reports no dividend payments at all (no PaymentsOfDividends fact exists for the company). So Coca-Cola sits in the middle of its large-cap beverage peers - well above PepsiCo but below Keurig Dr Pepper, and far above Monster, which returns capital only through buybacks. Two points of caution: KO's 2024 net income was depressed by the fairlife contingent consideration and IRS tax-litigation deposit effects, which flatters its payout ratio, and KDP's 2024 net income also fell sharply year over year (from $2,181 million in 2023), inflating its ratio; on 2023 net income KDP's payout would have been about 52%. On a dividends-per-share over diluted-EPS basis PepsiCo's FY2024 ratio is 76.7% ($5.33 / $6.95), consistent with the cash-flow calculation. These figures come from the companies' FY2024 annual-report XBRL facts rather than from reading a specific document, so no accession numbers are cited.

In its Q1 2024 shareholder letter, filed as Exhibit 99.1 to the 8-K of 9 May 2024 (accession 0001794669-24-000014), Shift4 broke its 2024 guidance down by quarter for the first time and guided Q3 2024 end-to-end payment volume to $46.0 billion to $48.0 billion, a midpoint of $47.0 billion. Actual Q3 2024 end-to-end payment volume was $43,483.9 million, i.e. $43.48 billion, per the key performance indicators table in the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2024 (accession 0001794669-24-000033). That is $3.52 billion below the midpoint, or -7.5% ((43.484 - 47.0) / 47.0). It also fell short of the bottom of the guided range by 5.5%. Note that volume still grew 56% year over year (from $27.93 billion in Q3 2023), so the shortfall was against guidance rather than a decline in the business.
